# domain/payments

> The payments domain takes card payments through Stripe, records every money movement in a double-entry ledger, credits shops when orders are paid, and pays shops out weekly through Stripe Connect.

`packages/backend/libs/domains/payments` · 28 files · 3 handlers

## How it works

A buyer's payment request arrives on the `payments.requests` topic, and "[Charging a card through Stripe](../../concepts/domain-payments/charging-a-payment.md)" charges the card once and saves the result using the "[Payment records and DTO service](../../concepts/domain-payments/payment-records.md)". If a payment ends up stuck, "[Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN](../../concepts/domain-payments/resolving-unknown-payments.md)" asks Stripe what really happened, and "[Daily Stripe reconciliation](../../concepts/domain-payments/daily-reconciliation.md)" double-checks our records against Stripe every night. When an order is paid, "[Settling paid orders to shops](../../concepts/domain-payments/settling-orders-to-shops.md)" credits each shop's share, and it does this through "[Recording money in the ledger](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md)". The ledger event feeds "[Shop balance and payout history reads](../../concepts/domain-payments/shop-balance-read-model.md)", which serve balances from Redis. "[Weekly seller payouts](../../concepts/domain-payments/weekly-seller-payouts.md)" then turns balances into [`Payout`](../../concepts/domain-payments/weekly-seller-payouts.md) rows and sends them via Stripe Connect. "[Ledger partitions and invariant checks](../../concepts/domain-payments/ledger-maintenance.md)" keeps the ledger healthy by creating partitions and checking that entries sum to zero.

## Topics

- [Charging a card through Stripe](../../concepts/domain-payments/charging-a-payment.md): Consumes `payments.requests` from Kafka, runs [`PaymentService`](../../concepts/domain-payments/charging-a-payment.md) with idempotency keys and [optimistic stock deduction](../../concepts/domain-payments/optimistic-stock-deduction.md), publishes results via outbox, routes failures to a DLQ, and refunds via saga if stock runs out.
- [Payment records and DTO service](../../concepts/domain-payments/payment-records.md): The `Payment` Sequelize model with statuses (including `UNKNOWN`) and scopes, plus [`PaymentDtoService`](../../concepts/domain-payments/payment-records.md) for CRUD and query access to payments.
- [Recording money in the ledger](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md): Double-entry bookkeeping in [`LedgerService`](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md): journals must sum to zero, entries are immutable [`LedgerEntry`](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md) rows, and each posting emits [`JournalPosted`](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md) through the outbox in the same transaction.
- [Settling paid orders to shops](../../concepts/domain-payments/settling-orders-to-shops.md): [`SettlementListener`](../../concepts/domain-payments/settling-orders-to-shops.md) reacts to `order.paid`, splits the net amount across shops by largest-remainder allocation, and posts the journal exactly once using a UUIDv5 `journalId` and an advisory lock.
- [Shop balance and payout history reads](../../concepts/domain-payments/shop-balance-read-model.md): [`BalanceProjector`](../../concepts/domain-payments/shop-balance-read-model.md) applies `ledger.journal_posted` events to Redis balances via a Lua script. [`FinanceController`](../../concepts/domain-payments/shop-balance-read-model.md) serves `GET /shops/:shopId/balance` and `/payouts`, falling back to the ledger.
- [Weekly seller payouts](../../concepts/domain-payments/weekly-seller-payouts.md): The `payouts.run-weekly` and `payouts.send` jobs create one [`Payout`](../../concepts/domain-payments/weekly-seller-payouts.md) per shop per week, transfer through Stripe Connect, and reverse the ledger journal on definite failures.
- [Resolving payments stuck in UNKNOWN](../../concepts/domain-payments/resolving-unknown-payments.md): The `payments.resolve-unknown` job runs every 5 minutes, queries Stripe by idempotency key for `UNKNOWN` payments, settles them through the ledger, and gives up after 60 minutes.
- [Daily Stripe reconciliation](../../concepts/domain-payments/daily-reconciliation.md): The `payments.reconcile-daily` job runs at 02:30 UTC, streams Stripe charges, compares them with the ledger by idempotency key, and records mismatches. It is idempotent per provider and day.
- [Ledger partitions and invariant checks](../../concepts/domain-payments/ledger-maintenance.md): [`LedgerMaintenanceJobs`](../../concepts/domain-payments/ledger-maintenance.md) runs `ledger.ensure-partitions` monthly to pre-create partitions and `ledger.verify-invariants` daily to check that the book and recent journals sum to zero.

## Key concepts

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Ledger journal | A balanced set of double-entry [`LedgerEntry`](../../concepts/domain-payments/recording-money-in-ledger.md) rows posted together; entries are immutable. |
| `ledger.journal_posted` | Event emitted in the same transaction as a journal; the balance projection consumes it. |
| UNKNOWN payment status | A payment whose Stripe outcome is unclear; a job later resolves it by idempotency key. |
| Idempotency key | Key sent to Stripe so a charge happens once; also used to match payments during reconciliation. |
| Settlement | On `order.paid`, net amount (total minus platform fee) is split across shops and credited in the ledger. |
| Payout | A weekly transfer of a shop's balance, created by `payouts.run-weekly` and sent by `payouts.send`. |

## Gotchas

- Balances come from a Redis projection fed by `ledger.journal_posted`, so they can lag the ledger.
- Ledger entries are immutable; corrections, such as payout reversals, are new journals, not edits.
- Payouts are two steps: `payouts.run-weekly` moves money in the ledger, then `payouts.send` calls Stripe. The ledger is reversed only if Stripe definitely refuses.
- Payments stuck in UNKNOWN are not failures; `payments.resolve-unknown` settles them through the ledger so orders react normally.
- The domain both publishes and consumes `ledger.journal_posted`, so check for loops when you change the listeners.
